title: Lateral Flow Buildup
author: Jorge Fernandez Mendez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8h2ht8e
materials: After the 10 minutes, remove the tubes from the thermoblock, and place them quickly on ice. Let them chill for other 10 minutes. That will allow the DNA to acquire the most favorable thermodynamic conformation.
After the last deposition of reagents, let the membrane to completely dry, keeping it overnight at 4ºC in a dessicator.

steps.title: Prepare Nitrocellulose Membranes
steps.instruction: Cut and label nitrocellulose FF80HP membrane strips for the test and control dots.

substeps.instruction: Cut 4 pieces of nitrocellulose FF80HP membrane (5 mm wide x 40 mm long).
Label the plastic backing 'T' (Test) or 'C' (Control) at 15 mm and 25 mm from the bottom of the strip.
Alternate the order of T/C in two strips and C/T in the other two.

steps.title: Attach Cellulose Absorbent Pads
steps.instruction: Fix absorbent pads to the top of the membrane strips.

substeps.instruction: Cut 4 pieces of cellulose absorbent pad (6 mm wide x 12 mm long).
Fix pads to the top of the strips using laboratory paper tape, overlapping the membrane by 6 mm.
Ensure tape applies soft pressure to maintain contact between the pad and membrane.

steps.title: Denature Aptamer Suspensions
steps.instruction: Heat aptamer suspensions to denature the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 10 μL of each aptamer suspension into two separate 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Place tubes in a pre-heated thermoblock at 95 ºC for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Streptavidin-DNA Conjugates
steps.instruction: Conjugate the amino terminal modified DNA sequence with streptavidin.

substeps.instruction: Mix 10 μL of 100 μM amino terminal modified DNA sequence with 10 μL of 5 μg/μL streptavidin suspension in the Eppendorf tubes.
Repeat for both DNA sequences and label the tubes.
Incubate the tubes on ice for 1 hour.

steps.title: Dilute Conjugates
steps.instruction: Create a 1:6 dilution of the Streptavidin-DNA conjugates.

substeps.instruction: Prepare two additional Eppendorf tubes.
Dilute 2 μL of each Streptavidin-DNA conjugate tube into 10 μL of PBS buffer.

steps.title: Deposit DNA onto Membranes
steps.instruction: Apply the DNA dilutions to the T/C regions of the membranes.

substeps.instruction: Place strips horizontally on a flat surface and label them.
Assign one pair of strips (with different T/C dispositions) to receive the 1:6 dilution (8 μM) and the other pair to receive the 50 μM prepared suspension.
Slowly pipette 0.33 μL of the corresponding DNA dilution onto the proper T/C region for each of the four tubes.
Allow membranes to dry for approximately 15 minutes.
Repeat the deposition process three more times at the exact same points, totaling 1.2 μL per region.

steps.title: Prepare E. Coli-Aptamer Complex
steps.instruction: Incubate aptamer conjugated beads with E. Coli suspension.

substeps.instruction: Mix 200 μL of 1% wt aptamer conjugated beads with 400 μL of E. Coli prepared suspension.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Load Sample into 96-Plate
steps.instruction: Distribute the E. Coli-Aptamer complex into a 96-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 125 μL of the E. Coli-Aptamer conjugated beads into 4 wells of a 96-plate (500 μL total).

steps.title: Perform Sample Migration
steps.instruction: Allow the sample to migrate through the prepared membranes.

substeps.instruction: Fit each prepared membrane into the wells of the 96-plate.
Allow sample migration for 30 minutes until the sample is absorbed into the top absorbent pad.

steps.title: Block Membranes
steps.instruction: Block the membranes to prevent non-specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Immerse the prepared membranes in 0.2% BSA suspension for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Visualize Results
steps.instruction: Observe the membrane for visible colored spots.
